keyPoints: CLAUDE.md holds persistent natural-language instructions, read at session start, layered enterprise → user → project root → nested subdirectory (narrowest scope that should always apply wins).
settings.json configures the deterministic side — tool permissions, allow/deny lists, hooks, env vars, model selection; settings.local.json holds personal uncommitted overrides.

Components divide up: Rules are persistent constraints, Skills are packaged instructions loaded on matching tasks, Commands are on-demand slash prompts, Agents are delegated workers with their own context, Agent Memory persists knowledge across sessions.
Headless mode is the mechanism for non-interactive, scripted, and CI-driven runs; `/init` bootstraps a project CLAUDE.md from the codebase.
Interrupted work is recovered through session resumption, not by rebuilding context by hand.
objectives.watchFor: CLAUDE.md is loaded into context every session, so letting it grow into a dumping ground wastes tokens and dilutes the instructions that matter.

question.stem: A team wants Claude Code to run their release checklist unattended each night from CI. Which mechanism fits?
options: A custom slash command invoked at the start of each session
Headless mode invoked by the CI scheduler
A CLAUDE.md instruction describing the nightly checklist
An auto-approval mode left running in an interactive session
question.answerWhy: Unattended, scheduled execution is precisely what headless mode provides, driven by an external scheduler or CI pipeline. Slash commands are on-demand shortcuts inside a session, CLAUDE.md supplies guidance rather than triggering runs, and leaving an interactive session in auto-approval mode is neither scheduled nor safely bounded.
